title: GazeSpace Studio — Eye Tracking & 3D Gaze
summary: Windows eye- and pupil-tracking studio with subject-calibrated screen gaze, 3D workspace mapping, camera SDK adapters, session replay, reporting, and tested portable builds.
challenge: Turn camera imagery into stable, bounded screen and 3D gaze coordinates while controlling jitter, drift, stale frames, device faults and calibration integrity.
approach: Built a Windows desktop and CLI around OpenCV pupil processing, MediaPipe iris/head landmarks, subject-specific 16-target screen and measured 3D calibration, world-space ray/surface intersection, filtering, recording/replay, reports, and local SDK/API integration. Validated source and frozen software through Windows CI and camera-SDK emulation; real-rig accuracy remains to be measured.

caseStudy.status: Windows software verified · physical camera, human gaze accuracy and original-client integration pending

facts.label: Full Windows tests
facts.context: SDK-enabled release job; zero failures or skips

facts.label: Platform test jobs
facts.context: Windows + Linux, Python 3.11/3.12; optional SDK tests isolated

facts.label: Packaged simulation
facts.context: Generated pupil frames; not human gaze measurements

facts.label: Desktop workspaces
facts.context: Frozen Qt interface and bundled font rendering checked

deliverables: Native Windows Studio and command-line applications; two integrity-checked unsigned portable distributions.
Pupil ellipse detection, iris/face landmark features, blink rejection, head pose and image-quality diagnostics.
OpenCV USB/UVC capture, configurable exposure/gain/frame settings, Basler pypylon adapter, optional aligned-depth RealSense path.
Guided 16-target screen calibration, independent 9-point validation, drift checks, camera intrinsics and 3D-target training.
Camera-to-world transforms, gaze rays, bounded 3D surfaces, stereo/depth helpers and interactive workspace views.
Recording, replay, AOI dwell, gaze heatmaps, jitter analytics, and offline HTML/JSON/CSV reports.
Reusable Python integration adapter, authenticated localhost REST/WebSocket telemetry, Windows CI and acceptance documentation.
evidence: Windows Server 2025 release CI: 225 automated tests passed with no failures, errors or skips.
Linux/Windows Python 3.11/3.12 matrix: four successful jobs; two optional SDK tests skipped per ordinary matrix job and exercised in release.
Frozen MediaPipe inference: 478 facial landmarks and both iris observations on a reference photo; not gaze ground truth.
Basler official SDK emulator: Mono8, Mono12 and BGR8Packed capture, control readback and lifecycle checks; no physical camera implied.
Frozen Studio: all seven pages painted and font-glyph rendering tested; source and frozen synthetic sessions exported reports.
Both Windows ZIPs independently verified, including 3,837 decompressed files per archive.
pending: Physical IR/global-shutter camera, lens, IR illumination, driver, USB transport and RealSense/depth-device performance not yet measured.
Human pupil/head-pose ground truth, screen/3D gaze accuracy, real-person jitter/drift, and end-to-end sensor-to-display latency not yet measured.
Final integration into a client's existing Windows codebase, client acceptance and publisher signing not yet performed.
